instruction: Navigate to Chrome's appearance settings to customize how your browser looks.

metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome appearance settings. Uses existing is_expected_active_tab_approximate metric to check if the active tab URL matches chrome://settings/appearance. Similar complexity to original task - single navigation action to Chrome internal settings page.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_active_url_from_accessTree extracts the active tab URL from the Chrome address bar via accessibility tree, which is the right state to verify
Metric comparison logic is correct: is_expected_active_tab_approximate strips query parameters from both URLs and compares them, which is appropriate for Chrome settings pages
Coverage is complete: the evaluator checks the only requirement in the instruction - that the user navigated to chrome://settings/appearance
Expected value is semantically correct: chrome://settings/appearance is the correct and stable Chrome internal URL for the appearance settings page
Data flow is sound: URL string from getter → metric strips query params → exact comparison with expected URL
Practical feasibility confirmed: Chrome internal URLs are stable, accessibility tree can reliably capture address bar content, no UI state dependencies requiring postconfig
